chapter_theme: Pattinathar's third Koyil Thiruvagaval, one unit built on the word அடைக்கலம், refuge, said eighteen times. The poet takes refuge in the Siva who held the ocean's poison in his throat, subdued Death with his foot and holds Brahma's skull in his left hand; then he lays out what he brings to that refuge, a dream life, a dirty mind, a thought born of anava mala and nesting in it like a worm in fat, and the whole roll of faults from deceit and envy to murder and fear, the three gunas and the five senses; and then the body that holds them, a hut the bird of life flies from, bound with bone and nerve and thatched with fat, a pot of mala, a pit of rice and sorrow, a cage of murderous weapons, a smith's bellows for the fire of anger, a cage of the five bird-senses, a top on the rope of desire, a windmill spinning for coins, a cart-wheel rolled over the void, a ship driven by the wind of lust into the sea of birth, a body that trembles when the Arbiter comes. When he lays it down as a corpse and sets out, he asks refuge at the lotus feet, and closes with the bull-rider, the unblinking-eyed, the one easy to devotees, the sea of mercy who dances in the hall of Tillai.
structure_note: Three parts: the Lord's deeds with the refrain (lines 1 to 8), the roll of the mind's faults (padirum, paavamum ... idumbaiyum piniyum), and the body catalogue in -ஐ accusatives that all depend on the single verb at line 42, பிணமெனப் படுத்தி யான் புறப்படும் பொழுது, when I lay it down as a corpse and set out; then the closing refrain. The body catalogue shares phrases with the second agaval (ஆசைக் கயிற்றிலாடு பம்பரம், சோற்றுத் துருத்தி, இருவினை).

302.reading: The poet takes refuge in the Siva who held in his throat the fierce poison churned from the milk ocean, who subdued the cruel-sceptred Death with a lifted foot, who tore off a head of Brahma, maker and owner of the whole world, and holds it in his left hand, the rich lord of the golden hall; and lays before him the dream-like life that spends itself along the mind's road, the dirty mind that knows no great meaning, the thought born of anava mala and writhing in it like a worm in fat, deceit, sin, blameworthy thinking, error, envy, miserly false oaths, guile, lies, great anger, strife, murder, baseness, enmity, fear, rashness and trembling, the folly of the three gunas and the bewilderment of the five senses, trouble and disease, all packed into the body: a hut from which the bird that is life flies off, bound at the middle with bone and nerve and thatched with fat flesh, leaking, a hut of red blood and small worms, a pot of mala-body, a bag of many bodies, an endless pit of rice and sorrow, a cage where many murderous weapons lie, a rubbish heap of weary deeds, a torn sack leaking the goods of the planets, a smith's bellows that kindles the fire of anger, a cage where the birds of the five senses roost, a hollow tree where cares breed, a top spinning on the rope of desire, a windmill whirling for coins and money, a wheel confused by the deeds of its children, a cart-wheel rolled across the great void, a cruel ship that enters the sea of birth with a cargo of sin, is tossed by the wind of lust and makes the shore by the way of ruin, a grass boat moving in the shackle of the two deeds, a body that shudders when the Arbiter comes calling: when he lays this down as a corpse and sets out, he asks refuge at the lotus of the Lord's feet; refuge with the god of the white bull that charges like a thunderbolt in the open, the unblinking-eyed king, the one easy to devotees, the sea of mercy who dances in the hall of Tillai of the Vedic Brahmins and whom gods and sages praise; refuge, king of the hall, with you.
302.nuance: The grammar carries the meaning: some thirty accusatives, the faults and the body's names alike, hang on one verb, 'when I lay it down as a corpse and set out', so that what is handed over at the refuge is everything the poet is, not a purified self. ஆணவ மலத்து உதித்து, born of anava mala, is the Siddhanta origin of the mind's own thought, and the worm in fat (நிணவைப் புழு) its figure. உயிரெனும் குருவி விட்டோடும் குரம்பை, the hut the bird of life flies from, is the Kural's image at 338 reversed, the body named from the bird's leaving. பலவுடற் புட்டில், a bag of many bodies, is loose: perhaps the body of many parts, or the body that has worn many bodies. கோள்சரக்கு, the goods of the planets, may be the planets' influence or a corrupt phrase for கோழைச் சரக்கு, phlegm. மறையவர் தில்லை, Tillai of the Brahmins, places the dance among the three thousand Dikshitars without comment, unusual in a Siddhar text that elsewhere attacks the twice-born.

links.note: The Kural says the friendship of body and life is like a bird flying off and leaving its nest (குடம்பை) behind; Pattinathar names the body a hut (குரம்பை) from which the bird that is life flies off, in the middle of his catalogue. Both use the one bird and the left nest; Pattinathar makes it one name among forty for what he is laying down.

Tirumular says to take refuge in the shade of the Pure One's holy feet and the leaping sea of deeds will not reach you; Pattinathar asks refuge at the lotus of the feet when he lays down the body that sailed the sea of birth with a cargo of sin. Both place the refuge at the feet and both set it against a sea of karma.

The second and third agavals share the top spinning on the rope of desire (ஆசைக் கயிற்றிலாடும் பம்பரம்), the bellows for rice, the casket or shackle of the two deeds and the ship of disease or of birth; the second ends 'enough, enough' and asks to be ruled, the third adds the roll of the mind's faults and ends in refuge. The second describes the body, the third hands it over.

new_concepts.gloss: refuge: the act of placing oneself, faults and body included, under the Lord's protection, said at his feet
new_concepts.label_source: The unit's own word, repeated eighteen times (அடைக்கலம், நின் அடைக்கலம், அடியநின் அடைக்கலம், அடைக்கல முனக்கே) and once as அபயம்

source_issues: Line 25 பலவுடற் புட்டிலைத் and line 29 கோள்சரக் கொழுகும் are hard to construe and may be corrupt (see the verse's nuance).
Line 13 ஆணவ மலத்துதித் தளைந்ததி னுளைத்திடும் is spaced across word boundaries (மலத்து உதித்து அளைந்து அதினுள் ஐத்திடும், or similar); the division is the source's.
Line 36 மயங்குங் திகிரியைக் has a sandhi fault (மயங்குந் திகிரியை expected).
